title: Run input, output and errors live in S3, not in the catalog
description:
`ProcedureRun.input`, `normalizedInput`, `output` and `error` hold whole JSON bodies in DynamoDB today, against the standing rule that DynamoDB is the catalog and text lives in S3. Move them to one attachment per run (the existing `ModelAttachment` path, owner kind `procedure_run`). The row keeps `resultSummary` and `errorSummary` as short fields and the attachment key. Readers (the console run view, `automations runs`, the Stage Bot engine reading `output.version`) read the attachment. Existing rows are converted once by a command; there is no reader for both shapes afterwards.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A new run row holds no body, only keys and short summaries.
- The console and CLI show the same output as before.
- The conversion command run twice changes nothing.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- run-bodies-in-s3.feature: a run row holds no output text; the run view shows the output read from S3; converting twice is a no-op; a run whose attachment is missing says so plainly.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** Amplify data schema (fields removed after conversion), storage access rule for the new owner kind.

**Part of:** Wake contract and run outcomes. Slice code A4 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text: Scoping note (2026-11-20): this is several PRs, not one. Writers of input/normalizedInput/output/error: the Python runner (cloud_procedures.update_cloud_procedure_run_record and the start mutation), amplify/functions/procedure-action/handler.ts (start: input, normalizedInput), amplify/functions/assignment-action/handler.ts (retry copies normalizedInput; executeImmediateProcedureRun writes output). Readers: automations.py (run detail, output and error), priming_export.py (output.story), story_commands.py (stage bot output), assignment-action handler (normalizedInput), automation-view/wire.ts, and the console run view. Needed first: owner kind procedureRun and a run_body role in model-attachment-upload (ALLOWED_OWNER_KINDS, ownerModelName, model_attachments.MODEL_ATTACHMENT_OWNER_MODELS), plus the storage rule. Proposed order: (1) owner kind and role, one read/write helper (run_bodies.py) with a missing-attachment error; (2) move the Python runner and CLI/automation readers; (3) the two TypeScript writers and readers; (4) the one-time idempotent conversion command; (5) a later release drops the four fields. Steps 2 and 3 must land in one release so no reader has to handle both shapes. Not started: the runner writes through AppSync with IAM, and I could not confirm in the cloud that its role may call the attachment upload mutation; that needs checking first.
